newsitem.title: USA: MSRB to release key reading on pay to play rule.
newsitem.headline: MSRB to release key reading on pay to play rule.

text.p: The Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board will announce an important interpretation shortly on how bond dealers are to apply the board's "pay-to-play" rule once someone in a firm gives an inappropriate political contribution, the board's chairman said on Monday.

"The board believes quite strongly that a dealer subject to the two-year ban should conduct no new business, Roger Hayes said. "And for any old business already under contract, (the dealer) would not be permitted to receive any additional compensation."

Hayes, managing director of municipal finance for NationsBanc Capital Markets Inc., discussed the interpretation in a press briefing with reporters. The board debated the issue last week at its quarterly board meeting in Hawaii.
Enacted in April 1994, the board's pay-to-play rule G-37 bars muni dealers that make contributions to issuer clients from engaging in negotiated business for two years with those governments.
